candidates: When adding or modifying interactive resize drag handles (e.g. the `Drag` component in `code/core/src/manager/components/layout/Drag.tsx`), verify that the element is fully keyboard-accessible: include a `:focus-visible` style equivalent to the `:hover` reveal, add `tabindex={0}` so the element is reachable by keyboard, and implement arrow-key handlers (wired into the same resize logic used by pointer events in `useDragging.ts`) so users who cannot operate a mouse can still resize panels.
Proofread string literals in Storybook `step()` descriptions and other test/story prose for typos and extraneous whitespace (e.g. double spaces) before submitting.

When defining a component with `React.memo`, keep the Props interface name, the internal function name passed to `React.memo`, and the exported variable name mutually consistent (e.g. `React.memo<PanelContainerProps>(function PanelContainer(...))`). Mismatched names — such as a `PagesContainerProps` interface or a `PagesContainer` function name on a component exported as `PanelContainer` — cause confusion during maintenance.

When introducing a new wrapper element inside an existing styled component's JSX, audit any `& > element` (direct-child) CSS selectors in the parent's styled definition; a new intermediate wrapper silently breaks the selector. Move the affected rule to the new wrapper's styled definition (or broaden the selector) so the intended styles still apply.
